question: The wavelengths missing in the absorption spectrum of a gas are found to be the same as some bright lines in its emission spectrum. Explain this observation.

options.A: Atoms absorb only certain definite wavelengths from continuous radiation and emit radiation at the same allowed wavelengths when excited. Therefore, wavelengths missing as dark absorption lines correspond to bright emission lines of the same gas.
options.B: Dark absorption lines and bright emission lines occur at unrelated wavelengths because absorption and emission involve different atoms.
options.C: The dark lines are caused by reflection of white light and do not relate to the gas emission spectrum.
options.D: The gas absorbs every wavelength but emits only one wavelength, so matching is accidental.
